function.mechanism: SO2-releasing sulfite chemistry provides reducing/antioxidant and antimicrobial effects and can inhibit enzymatic browning in relevant foods.

adi.basis: EFSA 2022 sulfite follow-up withdrew the temporary group ADI (0.7 mg/kg bw/day) because toxicity data were insufficient; E225 was not explicitly listed in the additives covered on the visited EFSA pages.

efsa.key_finding: For the sulfite group assessed by EFSA in 2022, existing ADI was withdrawn and MOE analysis indicated safety concerns for high consumers.

fda.notes: Listed under GRAS substances with GMP and category-specific maxima (as SO2), including 0.04% for beverages/beverage bases, 0.1% for preserved cherries and several condiment/sweetening categories, and 0.05% for frozen/liquid potatoes; related processing conditions are described in 21 CFR 173.325.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA entry for potassium sulfite (INS 225) reports a group ADI of 0-0.7 mg/kg bw, expressed as sulfur dioxide.

concerns.summary: Recent clinical review literature highlights sulfites as relevant allergens/contact sensitizers, with susceptible individuals at higher risk of reactions.
Sulfite-focused food toxicology review and mechanistic literature describe possible dysbiotic and gastrointestinal concerns, with direct evidence still limited and heterogeneous.

Experimental sulfite-class studies (e.g., sodium bisulfite) reported oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling in intestinal models, supporting mechanistic caution but not proving risk at all regulated dietary exposures.

no_concern_confirmed: IARC lists sulfites and sulfur dioxide as Group 3 (not classifiable as to carcinogenicity to humans).
No separate IARC agent entry for potassium sulfite was identified in the visited classification dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2022 communication reported MOE-based safety concern for high consumers and cited potential exceedance margins up to 12.5% (children) and 60% (adults) in the assessed sulfite context.

risk_assessment.rationale: Potassium sulfite remains permitted in major frameworks (FDA GRAS and JECFA group ADI), but sulfite-class risk evaluation in EFSA indicates unresolved uncertainty and high-consumer concern, and hypersensitivity evidence is credible in susceptible groups. This supports a moderate, caveat-heavy risk level rather than risk_free/limited or high.
key_factors: FDA GRAS listing with specific conditions (21 CFR 182.3798)
JECFA group ADI 0-0.7 mg/kg bw for sulfites including INS 225
EFSA sulfite follow-up withdrew temporary ADI and flagged high-consumer concern
IARC Group 3 classification for sulfites/sulfur dioxide
Human allergenicity/hypersensitivity concern in susceptible populations
